title: SRE Evidence Capture and Incident Chronicle
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a standardized, minimal-yet-sufficient evidence capture format (the Incident Chronicle) and an operational procedure for collecting, preserving, and auditing telemetry and artifacts during SRE incidents. The goal is to enable fast, accurate triage, reproducible forensics, and reliable post-incident analysis while minimizing oncall cognitive load.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all model-serving and inference control-plane incidents with SLO impact >= 1% burn in a 1-hour window or any customer-impacting outage.
- Intended audience: oncall SREs, responders, incident commanders, service owners, and postmortem authors.
- Not a replacement for existing runbooks; this prescribes evidence primitives and a lean chronicle artifact to attach to incident reviews.

Key principles
--------------
- Timeliness: capture essential artifacts in the first 10 minutes.
- Determinism: evidence should be reproducible where possible (commands, timestamps, node IDs).
- Completeness: preserve provenance (who captured what, why).
- Least privilege: redact secrets automatically; sensitive artifacts get restricted access.

Incident Chronicle (artifact) - canonical fields
------------------------------------------------
Provide a single, small JSON or Markdown document (the Chronicle) attached to the incident ticket (JIRA/ServiceNow). The Chronicle is purposely compact. Required fields:

1) incident_id: human-readable incident identifier (e.g., INF-2026-0423)
2) timeline_start_utc: ISO-8601 timestamp when responder first observed problem
3) observed_signals: short bullet list of primary alerts/metrics (name and short metric sample)
4) impact_summary: one-sentence customer and SLO impact statement
5) initial_hypothesis: short sentence (e.g., "KV cache saturation on model-pool-a")
6) captured_artifacts: list of artifact keys (log segments, traces, dump paths)
7) capture_commands: exact commands used to collect artifacts (copy with args)
8) owner_oncall: name and pager handle of primary oncall
9) evidence_bucket: storage path with expiration policy
10) preservation_flags: list of retention/permission overrides (if any)
11) final_state: closed|mitigated|ongoing
12) chronicle_version: schema version (e.g., v1)

Example Chronicle snippet (Markdown form)
---------------------------------------
incident_id: INF-2026-0423
timeline_start_utc: 2026-02-12T15:07:00Z
observed_signals:
- generation-latency.p95 = 3.6s (baseline 0.7s)
- error-rate.tokenize = 0.9% (baseline 0.01%)
impact_summary: Canary traffic experiencing sustained tail latency causing canary SLO to burn 12% in 30m
initial_hypothesis: model hotstart OOM thrash in quantized serving path
captured_artifacts:
- /evidence/INF-2026-0423/host-12/systemd-journal-15m.log
- traces/INF-2026-0423/trace-3f2a.json
- snapshot/redis-keys-2026-02-12T15-12.json
capture_commands:
- ssh ec2-user@host-12 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2026-02-12 14:55" > /tmp/journal-15m.log'
- rtracer fetch --trace-id 3f2a --to /evidence/INF-2026-0423/trace-3f2a.json
owner_oncall: Aisha Patel (@aisha-oncall)
evidence_bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/INF-2026-0423/ (retention=90d)
preservation_flags: [keep, legal-hold=false]
final_state: mitigated
chronicle_version: v1

Evidence capture primitives (what to collect first)
--------------------------------------------------
Collect in priority order. If automation is available, rely on it but always attach the Chronicle.
1) Alert context and relevant Grafana panel snapshot (p95/p99, heatmap if available)
2) Traces for the offending request(s) (3 top traces by latency or error)
3) Short log slices (15 minutes before, during, 5 minutes after) for implicated hosts
4) Runtime memory snapshots (if safe) or memory pressure metrics (RSS, OOM count)
5) Scheduler/Kubernetes pod events and deployments in last 30 minutes
6) Cache/KV metrics and recent eviction counts
7) Inference runtime metrics: batch sizes, queue depth, token issuance rate
8) Config/feature flags changed in the last 24 hours (via config history)
9) Sample input triggering the issue (redacted for PII)

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- First Responder: generate Chronicle, collect top-3 artifacts, mark timeline_start_utc.
- Incident Commander: validate Chronicle, assign acquisition of any long-lived artifacts (heap dumps) and request retention overrides.
- Evidence Steward (SRE runbook role): ensure artifacts are uploaded to evidence_bucket, set ACLs, and record preservation_flags.
- Service Owner: provide domain context and confirm final_state before postmortem kick-off.

Step-by-step rapid capture procedure (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------------------
1) Create incident ticket and set severity tag.
2) Populate Chronicle required fields (incident_id, timeline_start_utc, observed_signals, owner_oncall).
3) Run automated proof-capture (if enabled): `rundoc capture --incident $INCIDENT_ID --profile rapid` (captures graphs and traces).
4) If automation unavailable, run the manual minimal commands below and paste into capture_commands.
5) Upload artifacts to evidence_bucket and attach Chronicle link to ticket.
6) Set preservation_flags if legal or escalated customer involvement is detected.

Manual minimal capture commands (copy/paste)
-------------------------------------------
- grafana snapshot: curl -X POST "https://grafana.internal/api/snapshots" -d '{\"dashboard\": \"$DASH_ID\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- traces: rtracer fetch --service runtime --limit 3 --from=2026-02-12T15:00 --to=2026-02-12T15:15 > /tmp/top-traces.json
- logs: ssh $HOST 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "$(date --utc --date='15 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"' > /tmp/runtime-logs-15m.log
- pod events: kubectl -n inference get events --field-selector lastTimestamp>=$(date -d '15 minutes ago' -Iseconds)

Retention, access control, and redaction policy
------------------------------------------------
- Default evidence retention: 90 days.
- Preservation flags allow 1-year or legal-hold: Evidence Steward escalates to Security/Legal.
- Sensitive artifacts (PII, customer-provided prompts) must be redacted before storing; automation will detect common PII patterns and mark artifact as restricted.
- ACLs: oncall SREs + service owner + evidence-steward have read access by default; Legal/IR can be added with request.

Audit and post-incident obligations
----------------------------------
- Within 48 hours: attach Chronicle to postmortem draft and list captured_artifacts with checksums.
- Within 7 days: Evidence Steward validates retention settings and documents any preservation_flags.
- For incidents that trigger external communications, redact and produce an external-friendly evidence summary separate from the Chronicle.
- Periodic audit: quarterly run to ensure evidence buckets have correct ACLs and retention policies.

Operational tooling integration checklist
--------------------------------------
- Ensure `rundoc capture --profile rapid` exists in the toolchain and is callable from the oncall workstation.
- Integrate with PagerDuty: create incident and automatically populate incident_id and owner_oncall into Chronicle template.
- Provide a Confluence template macro to attach Chronicle to the incident page.
- Build a Lambda that enforces evidence_bucket encryption and retention on object creation.

Appendix A — Incident Chronicle checklist (quick)
------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Incident ticket created and severity set
- [ ] Chronicle created with initial_hypothesis
- [ ] Top-3 traces captured and uploaded
- [ ] 15m logs from implicated hosts captured
- [ ] Grafana snapshot attached
- [ ] Evidence bucket path recorded in Chronicle
- [ ] Preservation flags set if needed

Appendix B — Example annotated capture_commands (for copy/paste)
---------------------------------------------------------------
ssh ec2-user@host-12 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2026-02-12 14:55" > /tmp/journal-15m.log && aws s3 cp /tmp/journal-15m.log s3://redwood-evidence/INF-2026-0423/host-12-journal-15m.log'
rtracer fetch --trace-filter 'span.service:runtime and span.duration>1000' --limit 3 --to s3://redwood-evidence/INF-2026-0423/top-traces.json
